title: Procedural Galaxy
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a spiral galaxy with 50000 particles, featuring a central bulge and parameter-adjustable spiral arms.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Mathematical Model]
(1) 4 main spiral arms (default): polar coordinates r = a*exp(b*θ), with particles angularly distributed along each arm and Gaussian random scatter superimposed.
(2) id="armCount": range 2–6, integer steps; rebuild particle positions when the number of spiral arms changes.
(3) id="spread": range 0.1–2.0, controls arm width/dispersion.
(4) Central bulge: additionally increase particle density at small r values.

[Rendering]
(5) BufferGeometry + PointsMaterial or custom ShaderPoints; vertex colors represent temperature: blue is hotter and red is cooler; point size may vary with random brightness (sizeAttenuation).

[Animation]
(6) Slowly rotate the entire galaxy around the Y-axis; the id="rotSpeed" slider controls angular velocity.

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  starCount: number,
  armCount: number,
  spread: number,
  rotSpeed: number,
  galaxyRadius: number,
  centerDensity: number,
  simTime: number
}

Output a single HTML file that can run by being opened directly in a browser.
physics_constraints: Temperature-like vertex colors, size by brightness
